source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, New Jersey campus publishes 23 MW of IT capacity, about 21 percent of the state's 111.3 MW of disclosed data center power and the second-largest published figure in New Jersey.

Disclosure in New Jersey is thin and concentrated. Forty-eight facilities are mapped across the state, but only five publish power specifications to the operator level, so the 111.3 MW total describes a small slice of the built footprint. Somerset alone accounts for roughly a fifth of it, which means the state's published capacity ranking is really a ranking of which operators choose to publish. The campus holds 185,000 square feet of technical space, and no certifications appear on the operator's specification page.

For AI specifically, the number that matters is power delivered to the building, because accelerator counts follow from it. At a typical training density of 40 kW per rack, 23 MW supports roughly 575 racks, or about 3,450 accelerators at 6 GPUs per rack. Those figures are arithmetic on an assumed density, not a measurement of what is installed. The suitability score of 64 is built from published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing, so it says nothing about growth.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. Grid capacity and interconnection for New Jersey are absent, so whether Somerset can draw more power, and therefore add compute, is unknown. The 43 other mapped facilities likely host additional power and hardware, but with no published specifications their contribution cannot be counted. The state's true AI-relevant capacity is at least 111.3 MW and could be considerably more.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
